coaching.title: Easy 5 mi Z2 + Strength
coaching.message: Calendar has Week 5, Day 2: easy 5 miles in Zone 2, HR 138-150, plus strength session 2 (eccentric and plyometric durability, core). 22 days to Julian Alps — taper starts now, so this is the last full strength load before volume comes down. Yesterday was 1,300 ft of descending focus, so legs carry some eccentric damage: keep the run genuinely conversational and do not let Cieneguilla's rolling terrain drag you into Zone 3. Run first, lift after, at least 4 hours apart if the day allows. On the strength side, prioritize quality over load — eccentric step-downs, split squats, calf raises — the Alps descents are won here, but nothing that leaves you sore into the weekend.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Short easy session, so no need for big pre-run carbs — 30-40g (banana, toast, or a gel) is enough to protect the strength work later. Sip 500ml with 500-700mg sodium during the run given Lima-area heat and humidity. The real target today is protein: 30-40g within an hour of the strength session and again at dinner, ~1.8g/kg across the day to support the eccentric repair. Total carbs around 300-350g today — you are still building glycogen into taper, so do not start cutting carbs as volume drops. That is the classic taper mistake.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Back-to-back day after a vert session with descending focus — quads will be the limiter. Ten minutes of calf, quad, and glute mobility post-strength, then legs up the wall for five. Sleep is the highest-leverage lever in taper: aim 8 hours tonight. If quad soreness is above a 4 out of 10 tomorrow morning, downgrade the next session rather than pushing through. From here to September 18 you cannot gain fitness, you can only lose it to fatigue or injury.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: Taper officially begins. The work is banked — everything from here is about arriving in Kranjska Gora fresh, not fitter. You will feel twitchy and undertrained over the next three weeks; that feeling is the plan working, not a warning. Use today's easy miles to rehearse the mental script for the Julian Alps climbs: settle in, power hike the steep grades without ego, and remind yourself that patience on the first 2,500m of vert is what leaves something in the legs for the final descent.
